response.sql: WITH matched AS (SELECT f.orderslink, o.ordertune, f.rebtotal, (f.rebrate - f.feerate) / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0) AS relgap FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault), base AS (SELECT AVG(rebtotal) AS baseline FROM matched), grp AS (SELECT orderslink, ordertune, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebate, AVG(relgap) AS avg_relative_gap FROM matched GROUP BY orderslink, ordertune) SELECT g.orderslink, g.ordertune, g.avg_rebate, g.avg_relative_gap, g.avg_rebate - b.baseline AS excess_over_baseline FROM grp g CROSS JOIN base b WHERE g.avg_rebate > b.baseline ORDER BY excess_over_baseline DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: The baseline is the mean of rebtotal over all matched fee rows (inner join to orders), so each fee record is weighted equally, not an average of group averages.
Fee records with feerate = 0 get a NULL relative gap (division by zero avoided with NULLIF), and AVG ignores those NULLs. Such records still count in the average rebate and the baseline.
orders.recordvault is unique (as documented), so the join does not duplicate fee rows.
